title: At the End: a Possessive Ending Meaning 'Its End'

sections.content: vég means 'end'. To say 'at the end of X', Hungarian attaches a possessive ending to vég meaning roughly 'its end' (végE), then adds the locative -n: végén. The noun that owns the end (utca, 'street') comes right before it, unmarked.

items.english: It's at the end of the street.

items.spanish: Az iskola az utca végén van.
items.english: The school is at the end of the street.

sections.content: Literally, 'utca végén' is 'street its-end-on' -- Hungarian marks the possession on vég itself (végE = its end), not with a separate word like English 'of'.
